newsitem.title: UK: CRICKET-TAYLOR, ELLIOTT GIVE AUSTRALIA IDEAL START.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-TAYLOR, ELLIOTT GIVE AUSTRALIA IDEAL START.

text.p: A century opening partnership between captain Mark Taylor and Matthew Elliott gave Australia a perfect start to the fifth Ashes test against England on Thursday.
The pair put on 117, with Taylor hitting 76 and Elliott stroking 69, as Australia took advantage of good batting conditions at Trent Bridge to reach 181 for two by tea.
Taylor, having won his fifth consecutive toss in the series, made his first half-century since his 129 in the first test at Edgbaston in June.
Australia's skipper eventually lost his off-stump to a fine delivery from Andy Caddick that swung into the left-hander.
Elliott had been first out when he got a thin inside edge to a delivery from Dean Headley and was caught low down by wicketkeeper Alec Stewart.
There was a modicum of swing, but nothing in the pitch for England's bowlers, six of whom had been used by lunch, when the score was 84 without loss.
They included the Hollioake brothers, Melbourne-born but England-raised Adam and Ben, who had been thrust into their test debut.
The brothers were the first picked by England since Peter and Dick Richardson in 1957, while Ben Hollioake, at 19, became the youngest England test player since Brian Close in 1949.
It was a daunting introduction to test cricket in only his 12th first-class game as his first three overs of medium pace went for 23 runs.
Headley seemed to have had Taylor lbw when he had made 18, and almost caused Elliott to play-on long before inducing him to give the merest snick to Stewart.

Taylor had batted a further half-an-hour before Caddick struck at 160. By then he had become only the sixth Australian to pass 6,000 runs in test cricket, while Elliott reached 500 for the series and 1,000 on the tour.
At tea the not out batsmen were Greg Blewett (25) and Mark Waugh (six).
Australia, leading 2-1 in the six-test series, need only draw here to keep the Ashes, as they are the holders.
